newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND TAKE UPPER HAND IN 3RD TEST VS NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND TAKE UPPER HAND IN 3RD TEST VS NZ.

text.p: England bundled out two more New Zealand batsmen after lunch to take the upper hand on the first day of their third and final cricket test on Friday.

But a fighting innings by New Zealand's stand-in skipper Stephen Fleming ensured that the Kiwis were not out of the game. New Zealand were 160 for four at tea, with Fleming on 38 and Adam Parore on nine.

After being sent in to bat, New Zealand lost two wickets in each session. Openers Bryan Young and Blair Pocock were dismissed for 11 and 22 respectively before lunch, and new cap Matt Horne and Nathan Astle departed in the second session of the day.
Horne batted impressively in getting to 42 before edging fast-medium bowler Darren Gough to Graham Thorpe at first slip.

Astle, who like Fleming made a century in the drawn first test last month, looked good in getting to 15 before he tried to cut offspinner Robert Croft and Nasser Hussain clutched a brilliant catch at slip.
Croft had taken two for 30 from 14 overs, with Gough and Dominic Cork having one for 32 and one for 53 respectively.
